statement: Every homologically primitive element g of the full rank-two free profinite group has centralizer of each nonzero integer power equal to its full procyclic closure, and that closure is self-normalizing. For each full unit mu and both actual negative torus cusp-reflection labels v_i, explicit transporters g_{mu,i} have exactly homology plus or minus [g]; all solutions of [a,v_i]=c^mu form the specified coset g_{mu,i} C_F(v_i). Preservation of the F-conjugacy class of such an a by the involution is equivalent to an outside element of its E-centralizer. In the two-section case this supplies a unique other-class commuting reflection; in the one-section case it supplies a unique outside square root. Explicit mutually inverse maps give the resulting full peripheral conjugators, yielding an exact existence criterion for the entire D61 parameter space without asserting nonemptiness.
depends_on: Cohomological dimension one and torsion-freeness of the full free profinite group; D58 exact negative extension and full section classes; D59 primitive transporter homology and C_F(v) contained in the closed derived subgroup; D60 explicit full torsion quotient; D61 full boundary generation test and standard extension maps
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The primitive character gives the exact centralizer injection, and the outside centralizer/root comparison retains the full profinite extension coefficient at every prime.
notes: A nontrivial element in the kernel of the primitive character centralizing g^n would give a closed Z_p squared subgroup with the nonzero p-primary component of g^n, contradicting cohomological dimension one. The E-centralizer has exact coordinates Zhat times {0,1} with t squared equal to g^kappa. Even dyadic kappa gives the unique commuting reflection; odd dyadic kappa is adjusted at every odd prime to a full unit and then inverted to construct the unique outside square root. The D60 character forces the split case for two section classes, while D59 and one-class conjugacy exclude outside torsion in the other case. The equations alpha(g') conjugate to g' remain unresolved; their existence is not inferred from abelianization, from these centralizer formulas, or from projectivity. The written continuation gives g_{mu,0}=c^((mu-1)/2)g and g_{mu,1}=c^((mu+1)/2)g^{-1}. It proves the exact transporter cosets and homology signs without rescaling c. The D60 character has value plus or minus one in the two-class case; the same parity calculation and full root construction apply. The resulting standard extension maps retain [X,Y] mapping to c^mu and v0 mapping to v_i. The converse uses the actual image of X or XY from D61. The resulting all-unit conjugacy-existence equation remains unresolved.
computational_checks: The full root coefficient and centralizer arguments are proved algebraically. The source standard-model commutator and intertwining word identities were already executed in code/part_c/torus_negative_parameters_d61.py. The new code/part_c/torus_unit_transporters_d62.py and adjacent JSON/stdout check both exact reflection-label transporter identities and their homology/parity for thirty-two odd integer exponents in the universal free-product normal form. No finite approximation is used to infer full group structure or the missing conjugacy.
